Rowan: quick problem: quota-driven degradations are fine, but we lack a clear contract for what exactly gets redacted vs sampled when a route flips to "minimal". want to align on policy before FF.
Kim: agree. propose a tiny matrix: metadata-only, truncated-body, no-attachments, reserved-eval-sample.
Devon: concrete: minimal = headers + route + fingerprint; standard = metadata + first 256 chars of response (redact patterns); strict = schema-only, lengths. keep a fixed eval_sample=0.1% across all levels.
Asha: note on attachments/embeddings: always treat as strict: store blob-id + salted-hash, never raw or partial in logs.
Rowan: how to implement without causing mid-request surprises? decision: compute privacy level at ingress and attach to request context. downstream services read that and apply redaction. no mid-request flips.
Kim: telemetry: emit events privacy_level_set and privacy_level_effective. metrics: privacy_level_over_time, redaction_hit_count, sampled_eval_count, partial_leak_detected.
Devon: console UX: route detail should show current privacy_level + last change reason (quota, manual override, admin). add button: "pin to ignore auto-degrade" (audited).
Asha: legal wants an immutable audit event when a route goes strict. include actor, reason, previous_level, tenant_id. no PII in the event.
Rowan: edge-case: if eval sample got selected pre-ingress decision (race), prefer safety: respect redaction unless explicit breakglass with audit.
Kim: rollout: FF -> 10% tenants, monitor eval_pass_rate and redacted_hit_rate. rollback if pass_rate drops >3% within 6h.
Devon: action items: Rowan -> RFC + data-contract; Kim -> add metrics + alert; Asha -> embed/attachment guidance; ops-bot -> create infra ticket for schema migration.
ops-bot: ticket created: INFRA-2048 add privacy_level to request schema.
Rowan: cool. I'll draft the RFC and wire examples for the console modal. update team in #eng-platform when ready.
